title: Patient specific Contrast Enhancement timing in Run-Off CTA Study
summary:
The study presented is a monocentric, single-arm, prospective, unblinded pilot study with a retrospective control cohort, ideally matched for age, sex, and clinical indication. 
Assessments by the investigators will be blinded.  Two radiologists will independently evaluate the vascular images (blinded-read).
There will be no follow-up.
Participation in the study is only during the routine scheduled CT scan and ends with imaging.
conditions: Disorders of arteries, arterioles and capillaries in diseases classified elsewhere

interventions.name:
If stenosis of the iliac-legal stromal pathway is clinically suspected, CT imaging with contrast is performed. Patients in the prospective arm will be studied with delayed KM administration.
Patients with standardized KM administration in the retrospective arm will be compared with these cases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinical suspicion of stenosis of the iliac-legal stromal pathway
Exclusion criteria:
- Contraindication to undergoing a computed tomography scan
- Refusal to participate in the study
- Age-adjusted normal serum creatinine or creatinine clearance > 30 ml / min / 1.73 m2 as a contraindication for safe contrast administration
